title: Trustworthy AI Helper - Build & Refine the Prompt (Part 1 Lab)
summary: Students turn their Week 5 Core design into a working prototype and improve it by changing one part of the prompt at a time, logging each version, change and effect.
objectives: Build a working prototype of the helper using the structured prompt and improved data.
Refine the prompt across versions to raise output quality, logging each change and its effect.

body: Now build it! Today you turn your design into a working helper and make it better by refining the prompt, one change at a time.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can build a working prototype of my helper.

terms.definition: A first working version you can test and improve.

sections.heading: Build, run, refine
body: Run your prompt on the improved data and read the output.
Judge it against your task. Then change one part of the prompt and run it again.
Changing one thing at a time tells you what actually helped.

worksheet.title: Week 5 - Lab - Worksheet | Trustworthy AI Helper - Build & Refine the Prompt (Part 1 Lab)

questions.prompt: Sam's prompt v1 is 'Suggest a book.' The output was a vague list. He wants his v2 to show him what actually helped. Which v2 is the best next step?

options.text: Using our class reading survey, suggest a book.
Using our class reading survey, suggest one book, give one sentence saying why, and keep it friendly.
Please could you kindly suggest a book for us? Thank you very much!

feedback.correct: Only one part of the prompt changed, so any improvement in the output can be pinned on naming the data.
feedback.incorrect: Changing several parts at once hides which one helped, extra politeness adds words but no precision, and changing the task means you are no longer testing the same helper.

questions.prompt: Match each change Sam made to his prompt with the effect you would expect it to have on the output.

left.text: Added 'name one book, not a list'
Added 'please be as helpful and friendly as you can'

right.text: The answer is now based on the class's own data instead of a general guess.
The answer is a single choice instead of several.
The answer now explains the reason behind the choice.
The prompt got longer, but the answer is no more useful.

feedback.correct: Each useful change targets one thing - the data, the number of answers, or the reasoning - while extra friendly words only make the prompt longer.
feedback.incorrect: Ask what each change tells the helper to do differently; a change that adds no new instruction changes the length of the prompt, not the quality of the output.

questions.prompt: Maya claims her v3 is better than her v2, and that her change is what made it better. Which of these count as good evidence for her claim? Select all that apply.

options.text: v3's output names one book, which is what her task asked for.
v3's prompt has more words in it than v2's.
v3's output gives a reason, so Maya can judge whether the choice makes sense.
Only one part of the prompt changed between v2 and v3, so Maya knows what caused the change.
v3's prompt sounds more polite than v2's.

feedback.correct: Better means the output meets the task and can be judged, and a single change is what lets Maya say which edit caused it.
feedback.incorrect: A longer or politer prompt is not evidence of a better output - the evidence is that the output now meets the task, can be judged, and followed one change you can point to.

questions.prompt: Omar changes three parts of his prompt at the same time and the output gets much better. True or false: he can still say which of the three changes caused the improvement.

feedback.correct: Right - with three edits made together any of them, or all of them, could be responsible, so he would have to test them one at a time.
feedback.incorrect: A better output only tells you the new prompt as a whole works better; to name the change that helped, you have to change one part at a time.

questions.prompt: Sam's log: v2 'Using our class reading survey, suggest a book' returned a list with no explanation. v3 'Using our class reading survey, suggest one book and give one sentence saying why' returned a single title with a reason. Complete the explanation: the change from v2 to v3 improved the output because it told the helper to name ___ book and to give a ___.

feedback.correct: Naming how many answers and asking for the thinking behind them is what turned a vague list into something the class can judge.
feedback.incorrect: Compare the two prompts word by word: v3 asks for one book rather than several, and asks the helper to say why it chose it.

formative.targets: Integrated mastery - SD (refine prompts to improve output quality and explain why)
formative.check: Prompt-refinement log (v1 to best) with a reasoned justification for the key change
formative.successCriteria: Iterates the prompt to a measurably better output and explains the causal reason for the improvement.
formative.evidence: Prompt-refinement log (Trustworthy AI Helper Log, Part 1 Lab).
